title: Embeddings and Vector Search Handbook
summary: Quick revision notes on embeddings, cosine similarity, vector databases, approximate nearest neighbour indexes, semantic versus keyword search and hybrid search, from mental model to production pitfalls.

chapters.title: Embeddings and the Vector Mental Model
points: An embedding is a fixed-length array of floats (e.g. 384, 768, 1536 dims) produced by a model so that similar meaning lands at nearby points
Meaning is encoded by position: 'car' and 'automobile' sit close, 'car' and 'banana' sit far apart
Dimensions have no human-readable meaning; only distances and angles between vectors are meaningful
Vectors from different models are incompatible: different spaces, different dimensions, never mix them in one index
Embed a query and documents with the same model; chunk long text first because models have a token limit and one vector blurs many topics

chapters.title: Similarity Metrics: Cosine, Dot Product, Euclidean
points: Cosine similarity = (a·b) / (|a||b|), range -1 to 1; measures angle and ignores vector length
Dot product = sum of a_i*b_i; equals cosine when vectors are L2-normalised to length 1, and is the fastest to compute
Euclidean (L2) distance = sqrt(sum (a_i-b_i)^2); smaller is closer, and it is sensitive to magnitude
Worked example: a=[1,0], b=[1,1] gives cosine = 1/(1*1.414) ≈ 0.71; a=[1,0], c=[0,1] gives cosine 0 (unrelated)
Mistake: using a different metric from the one the embedding model was trained for, or treating cosine distance (1 - cosine) as if it were similarity

chapters.title: Vector Databases and Core Workflow
points: A vector database stores vectors plus metadata and answers top-k nearest-neighbour queries; examples: pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus, FAISS (library, not a DB)
Ingest pipeline: split documents into chunks (≈200-500 tokens with overlap) → embed each chunk → upsert vector + id + metadata
Query pipeline: embed the query with the same model → search top-k by chosen metric → optionally filter by metadata → return chunks

Example pgvector: CREATE EXTENSION vector; CREATE TABLE docs(id serial, body text, emb vector(768)); SELECT body FROM docs ORDER BY emb <=> $1 LIMIT 5; (<=> cosine distance, <-> L2, <#> negative inner product)
Metadata filters (tenant, date, language) are applied with the vector search; filter-after-search can return fewer than k results

chapters.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbour Indexes
points: Exact (brute-force/flat) search compares the query to every vector: O(N·d), perfect recall, fine up to ~100k vectors
ANN trades a little recall for big speed: returns most true neighbours, not guaranteed all; quality is measured as recall@k

HNSW: layered proximity graph, greedy search from the top layer down; fast and high recall but memory-heavy; knobs M (links per node), efConstruction (build quality), efSearch (query-time breadth, higher = better recall, slower)

IVF: k-means clusters vectors into nlist cells and searches only the nprobe nearest cells; less memory, tune nprobe for recall; PQ (product quantization) compresses vectors to cut memory at some accuracy cost
Mistake: never measuring recall against a flat-search baseline, or building an IVF index before the table has enough representative data to train the clusters

chapters.title: Semantic, Keyword and Hybrid Search
points: Keyword search (BM25) matches exact terms weighted by term frequency and rarity; great for IDs, error codes, names, rare jargon; misses synonyms and paraphrase
Semantic search matches meaning via embeddings; finds 'cheap flights' for 'budget airfare' but can miss exact strings like 'ERR_4012' or a SKU
Hybrid search runs both and merges the ranked lists; Reciprocal Rank Fusion score = sum over lists of 1/(k + rank), with k≈60, avoids having to normalise incompatible scores
Typical production pipeline: hybrid retrieve top 50-100 → cross-encoder reranker → top 5 into the LLM; rerankers are accurate but too slow to run over the whole corpus
Mistakes: re-embedding with a new model without re-indexing everything, ignoring chunk size, and judging quality by eyeballing instead of a labelled query set with recall@k / MRR

chapters.title: Embeddings and Vector Search Cheat Sheet
points: Embedding = fixed-length float vector; same model for queries and documents; never mix models in an index
Cosine ignores length; dot product = cosine on normalised vectors; L2 is magnitude-sensitive; match the model's training metric
Pipeline: chunk → embed → upsert with metadata; query: embed → top-k → filter → rerank
Flat = exact and slow at scale; HNSW = fast, high recall, more RAM (tune efSearch); IVF = cluster pruning (tune nprobe); PQ = compression
Keyword (BM25) for exact tokens, semantic for meaning, hybrid with RRF (k≈60) for both; add a reranker on the top 50-100
Measure recall@k against a flat baseline and keep a labelled test query set
